meta_title: Area Bounded by x2=4y, y=2, y=4 | NCERT Ex 8.1 Q3
meta_desc: Step-by-step solution to NCERT Class 12 Ex 8.1 Q3: area bounded by x2=4y, y=2, y=4 and the y-axis, integrated w.r.t. y, plus a free 8-question quiz.

quiz.title: Area Using Integration Quiz (Ex 8.1 Q3)
quiz.intro: Eight questions on finding area with respect to y, area under a parabola and area between horizontal lines. Choose an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: Application of Integrals — area bounded by x2=4y, y=2 and y=4

questions.q: For the region bounded by x² = 4y and the y-axis between y = 2 and y = 4, which integral gives the area?
questions.explanation: In the first quadrant x = 2√y from x² = 4y. The strip is horizontal, so integrate x with respect to y from 2 to 4: ∫<sub>2</sub><sup>4</sup> 2√y dy.

questions.q: What is the exact area of the region bounded by x² = 4y, y = 2, y = 4 and the y-axis in the first quadrant?
Why do we integrate with respect to y here instead of x?
options: Because the area is negative otherwise
Because the y-axis is not a boundary
The bounding lines y = 2 and y = 4 are horizontal, so horizontal strips of width x are natural
Because x² = 4y cannot be solved for x
questions.explanation: The region is bounded above and below by horizontal lines, so a strip parallel to the x-axis has length x = 2√y and thickness dy — integrating w.r.t. y is the clean choice.

questions.q: The antiderivative of 2√y with respect to y is:
For the parabola x² = 4y, what is x when y = 4 in the first quadrant?
questions.explanation: x² = 4(4) = 16, so x = 4 (positive root for the first quadrant).

questions.q: What is the area under x² = 4y in the first quadrant between y = 0 and y = 2 (bounded by the y-axis)?
If the same parabola were bounded between y = 1 and y = 4, the area (w.r.t. y) would be:
questions.explanation: Area = (4/3) y<sup>3/2</sup> from 1 to 4 = (4/3)(4<sup>3/2</sup> − 1) = (4/3)(8 − 1) = 28/3 sq units.

questions.q: Which statement about area found by definite integration is correct here?
options: The integral must be made negative before it is an area
The area depends on which variable of integration you choose
The y-axis boundary means the lower limit must be 0
Because the region lies to the right of the y-axis, x = 2√y is positive throughout, so the integral gives the area directly
questions.explanation: The whole region is in the first quadrant where x ≥ 0, so 2√y ≥ 0 on [2, 4] and the definite integral is already the positive area.

faq.q: How do you find the area bounded by x² = 4y, y = 2, y = 4 and the y-axis?
faq.a: Solve the parabola for x in the first quadrant: x = 2√y. Since the boundaries y = 2 and y = 4 are horizontal, integrate x with respect to y: area = ∫ from 2 to 4 of 2√y dy.

faq.q: What is the final answer to NCERT Ex 8.1 Q3?
faq.a: The area is (4/3)(8 − 2√2) = (32 − 8√2)/3 square units, which is about 7.77 square units.

faq.q: Why integrate with respect to y rather than x in this problem?
faq.a: The region is capped by the horizontal lines y = 2 and y = 4, so a horizontal strip of length x = 2√y and thickness dy sweeps the region cleanly. Integrating w.r.t. y avoids splitting the area.

faq.q: Does the y-axis actually change the calculation?
faq.a: The y-axis (x = 0) is the left boundary of each horizontal strip, so the strip length is just x = 2√y measured from the axis. It confirms we take x from 0 out to the curve, not the region on the other side.
